text: In Vitruvius’s Roman watermill description, a toothed wheel on the waterwheel axle drives a smaller horizontal toothed wheel attached to the millstone. The paired gears transfer rotation from the horizontal waterwheel axle to the vertical millstone axis while a hopper feeds grain to the stones (Book X.5).
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Vitruvius, De architectura, Augustan Roman world, translated by Morris Hicky Morgan (1914), public-domain primary text; https://www.gutenberg.org/files/20239/20239-h/20239-h.htm . Verified primary context: Book X.5.2; chapter also specified in the stimulus.
